sentences.zh: 陳旭陳賢張興陳誌王友

translations.literal: Chen Xu, Chen Xian, Zhang Xing, Chen Zhi, Wang You
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xu; Chen Xian; Zhang Xing; Chen Zhi; Wang You

translations.literal: Chen Gui was a man of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui came from Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，從大將軍徐達平中原，授龍虎衛百戶，改燕山中護衛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, he followed the great general Xu Da in pacifying the Central Plain, was appointed a centurion in the Longhu Guard, and was transferred to the Yan Mountain Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign he followed Grand General Xu Da in pacifying the Central Plain, received appointment as a centurion in the Longhu Guard, and was then transferred to the Yan Mountain Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 從成祖出塞為前鋒，進副千戶。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Yan beyond the frontier as vanguard and was promoted to deputy chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the future Yongle Emperor on campaigns beyond the frontier as vanguard and was promoted to deputy chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 已，從起兵，積功至指揮同知。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed the prince in raising troops, and through accumulated merit rose to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the prince's rebellion and, through accumulated merit, rose to vice commander.

translations.literal: He returned to assist the heir apparent in holding the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to assist the heir apparent in defending the capital.

sentences.zh: 累遷都督僉事，封泰寧侯，祿千二百石。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became vice commissioner-in-chief, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Taining with an income of twelve hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to vice commissioner-in-chief, enfeoffed as Marquis of Taining, and granted an income of twelve hundred piculs.

translations.literal: He continued to assist the heir apparent in holding the capital as before.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to assist the heir apparent in defending the capital as before.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年董建北京宮殿，經畫有條理，甚見獎重。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle he supervised construction of the Beijing palaces; his planning was orderly and he was greatly rewarded and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 4 he oversaw construction of the Beijing palaces; his planning was methodical, and he won high praise.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝北征，偕駙馬都尉袁容輔趙王留守北京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor campaigned north; together with the imperial son-in-law commandant Yuan Rong he assisted the Prince of Zhao in holding Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the emperor marched north, he joined Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Yuan Rong in assisting the Prince of Zhao in holding Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十五年命鑄繕工印給珪，並設官屬，兼掌行在後府。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was ordered to cast a Works Office seal and give it to Gui, to establish an official staff, and concurrently to manage the rear headquarters at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the court ordered a Works Office seal cast for Gui, established a staff under him, and had him concurrently manage the rear headquarters at the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 十七年四月卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventeenth year he died at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of the seventeenth year, aged eighty-five.

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jing with the posthumous title Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jing and given the posthumous title Zhongxiang.

translations.literal: His son Yu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he followed the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he joined the northern campaign.

translations.literal: He violated military discipline, was imprisoned, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He violated military discipline, was thrown into prison, and died there.

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Zhong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son Zhong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 再傳至瀛，歿土木，贈寧國公，謚恭湣。

translations.literal: After two more generations the line reached Ying, who died at Tumu; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ning with the posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations later the line reached Ying, who died at Tumu; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ning and given the posthumous title Gongmin.

translations.literal: His younger brother Jing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jing succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianshun he was stationed in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 6 he took command in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年九月，瑤賊作亂，涇將數千人駐梧州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year Yao bandits rose in revolt; Jing led several thousand men and encamped at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following ninth month, when Yao rebels rose in revolt, Jing led several thousand men and encamped at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 是冬，大藤賊數百人夜入城，殺掠甚眾。

translations.literal: That winter several hundred Great Vine bandits entered the city by night and killed and plundered a great many people.
translations.idiomatic: That winter several hundred Great Vine bandits entered the city by night and killed and plundered on a large scale.

translations.literal: Jing held his troops and did not rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing held his troops back and did not come to the rescue.

translations.literal: He was recalled from the campaign, imprisoned, and sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from the field, he was imprisoned and sentenced to decapitation.

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon pardoned.

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

translations.literal: His son Huan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was stationed in Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign he took command in Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 中貴人多以所親冒功賞，桓拒絕之，為所譖，召還。

translations.literal: Many eunuchs had their favorites claim merit rewards falsely; Huan refused them, was slandered by them, and was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Many eunuchs had their favorites claim merit rewards falsely; Huan refused them, was slandered, and was recalled.

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

translations.literal: After several more generations the line reached Yanzuo; when Ming fell the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Several generations later the line reached Yanzuo; when the dynasty fell the title was abolished.

translations.literal: Zheng Heng was a man of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Heng came from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 父用，洪武時，積功為大興左衛副千戶。

translations.literal: His father Yong, in the Hongwu period, through accumulated merit became deputy chiliarch of the Daxing Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong, in the Hongwu period, rose through accumulated merit to deputy chiliarch of the Daxing Left Guard.

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of age, and Heng succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: When he sought retirement on grounds of age, Heng succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十五年，應募持檄諭韃靼，至斡難河。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Hongwu he answered a call for recruits, carried an edict to instruct the Tartars, and reached the Onon River.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 25 he answered a recruitment call, carried an edict to instruct the Tartars, and reached the Onon River.

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to vice commander of the Miyun Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to vice commander of the Miyun Guard.

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, he surrendered with the troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan's army rose, he surrendered with the troops under his command.

translations.literal: In the battle at Zhending he was first to scale the walls and was promoted to commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Zhending he was first over the wall and was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 襲大寧，至劉家口，諸將將攻關，成祖慮守關卒走報大寧得為備，乃令亨將勁騎數百卷旆登山，潛出關後，斷其歸路。

translations.literal: In the strike on Ning they reached Liujiakou; the generals were about to assault the pass, but the Prince of Yan feared the garrison would flee to warn Ning and allow it to prepare defenses, so he ordered Heng to lead several hundred crack horsemen, roll up their banners, climb the mountain, slip out behind the pass, and cut off their line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: On the strike toward Ning they reached Liujiakou. The generals were about to assault the pass, but the Prince of Yan feared the garrison would flee to warn Ning and allow it to prepare defenses, so he ordered Heng to lead several hundred crack horsemen, roll up their banners, climb the mountain, slip out behind the pass, and cut off their line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 急攻之，悉縛守關者，遂奄至大寧。

translations.literal: They pressed the attack urgently, bound all the pass defenders, and then swept on to Ning.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack hard, bound every defender at the pass, and then swept on to Ning.

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commander of the Beijing metropolitan command.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commander of the Beijing metropolitan command.

sentences.zh: 夜帥眾破鄭村壩兵，西破紫荊關，掠廣昌，取蔚州，直抵大同。

translations.literal: By night he led his troops to defeat the army at Zhengcun Dam, broke Zijing Pass to the west, raided Guangchang, took Weizhou, and drove straight to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: By night he led his troops to rout the army at Zhengcun Dam, broke Zijing Pass to the west, raided Guangchang, took Weizhou, and drove straight to Datong.

sentences.zh: 還戰白溝河，逐北至濟南，進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: He returned to fight at Baigou River, pursued north to Jinan, and was promoted to metropolitan vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to fight at Baigou River, pursued north as far as Jinan, and was promoted to metropolitan vice commander.

sentences.zh: 攻滄州，軍北門，扼餉道東昌。

translations.literal: In the assault on Cangzhou he encamped at the north gate and choked the supply route at Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Cangzhou he encamped at the north gate and choked the supply route at Dongchang.

translations.literal: He was defeated in battle, gathered the scattered troops, and withdrew the army to Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a defeat he gathered the scattered troops and withdrew the army to Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年戰夾河、槁城，略地至彰德，耀兵河上。

translations.literal: The next year he fought at Jiahe and Gaocheng, overran territory as far as Zhangde, and displayed his army's strength along the river.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he fought at Jiahe and Gaocheng, overran territory as far as Zhangde, and displayed his army's strength along the river.

translations.literal: He returned and encamped at Wan County.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and encamped at Wan County.

sentences.zh: 明年從破東平、汶上，軍小河。

translations.literal: The next year he followed in the capture of Dongping and Wenshang and encamped the army at Xiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he followed in the capture of Dongping and Wenshang and encamped the army at Xiaohe.

translations.literal: They were defeated in battle and Wang Zhen died.
translations.idiomatic: They were defeated in battle and Wang Zhen was killed.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆欲北還，惟亨與朱能不可。

translations.literal: All the generals wished to return north, but only Heng and Zhu Neng would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals wanted to withdraw north, but Heng and Zhu Neng alone refused.

sentences.zh: 入京師，歷遷中府左都督，封武安侯，祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: On entering the capital he was promoted in stages to left regional commander of the central command, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an with an income of fifteen hundred piculs, and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the capital he rose in stages to left regional commander of the central command, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an with an income of fifteen hundred piculs, and granted a hereditary patent.

translations.literal: He remained to hold Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: He remained behind to hold Beijing.

sentences.zh: 時父用猶在，受封爵視亨。

translations.literal: At that time his father Yong was still alive and received a noble title equal to Heng's.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his father Yong was still alive and received a noble title equal to Heng's.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，充總兵官，帥武成侯王聰、安平侯李遠備宣府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle he served as supreme commander, leading the Marquis of Wucheng Wang Cong and the Marquis of Ping'an Li Yuan to defend Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 he served as supreme commander, leading Marquis of Wucheng Wang Cong and Marquis of Ping'an Li Yuan to defend Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 亨至邊，度宣府、萬全、懷來形便，每數堡相距，中擇一堡可容數堡士馬者，為高城深池，浚井蓄水，謹瞭望。

translations.literal: When Heng reached the frontier he surveyed the advantages of terrain at Xuanfu, Wanquan, and Huailai; wherever several forts stood at intervals from one another, he chose among them one fort that could hold the troops and horses of several forts, built high walls and deep moats, dug wells to store water, and kept watch carefully.
translations.idiomatic: When Heng reached the frontier he surveyed the terrain at Xuanfu, Wanquan, and Huailai. Wherever several forts stood at intervals, he chose one that could hold the troops and horses of several forts, built high walls and deep moats, dug wells to store water, and kept careful watch.

sentences.zh: 寇至，夜舉火，晝鳴炮，並力堅守。

translations.literal: When bandits came they lit fires by night and fired cannon by day and defended together with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders came they lit beacon fires by night and fired cannon by day and defended together with all their strength.

translations.literal: His planning was thorough and complete; afterward no one could improve on it.
translations.idiomatic: His planning was thorough; afterward no one could improve on it.

sentences.zh: 三年二月召還，旋遣之鎮。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year he was recalled, and soon afterward was sent back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year he was recalled, and soon afterward was sent back to his command.

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year he prepared the frontier at Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year he prepared the frontier at Kaiping.

translations.literal: The next year the emperor campaigned north and ordered Heng to supervise transport.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor marched north and ordered Heng to supervise transport.

sentences.zh: 出塞，將右哨，追敗本雅失裏。

translations.literal: Beyond the frontier he commanded the right wing, pursued and defeated Buyanshirid.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the frontier he commanded the right wing, pursued, and defeated Buyanshirid.

translations.literal: The main army encountered Arughtai.
translations.idiomatic: The main army encountered Arughtai.

translations.literal: Heng led the troops forward first and inflicted a great defeat on him.
translations.idiomatic: Heng led the troops forward first and inflicted a crushing defeat.

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he stood at the head of all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the reckoning of merit he stood at the head of all the generals.

translations.literal: That winter he again went out to command at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he again took command at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 十二年復從北征，領中軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he again followed the northern campaign and led the central army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he again joined the northern campaign and led the central army.

sentences.zh: 戰忽失溫，追敵中流矢卻，復與大軍合破之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hulunbuir he was struck by a stray arrow while pursuing the enemy and fell back, then rejoined the main army and together defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Hulunbuir he was struck by a stray arrow while pursuing the enemy and fell back, then rejoined the main army and together they defeated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 二十年復從出塞，將左哨，帥卒萬人，治龍門道過軍，破兀良哈於屈裂河。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he again followed beyond the frontier, commanded the left wing, led ten thousand troops, cleared the Longmen route for passing armies, and defeated the Uriankhai at the Qulie River.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he again marched beyond the frontier, commanded the left wing, led ten thousand troops, cleared the Longmen route for passing armies, and defeated the Uriankhai at the Qulie River.

sentences.zh: 將輜重還，擊破寇之追躡者，仍守開平。

translations.literal: He led the baggage train back, defeated the bandits who pursued them, and again held Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: He led the baggage train back, defeated the raiders who pursued them, and again held Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 成祖凡五出塞，亨皆在行。

translations.literal: Of the Prince of Yan's five campaigns beyond the frontier, Heng was present at all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Yongle Emperor's five campaigns beyond the frontier, Heng was present at every one.

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was stationed at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was stationed at Datong.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年二月，頒制諭及將軍印於各邊總兵官。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Hongxi, imperial instructions and general's seals were issued to the supreme commanders on each frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Hongxi 1, imperial instructions and general's seals were issued to the supreme commanders on each frontier.

translations.literal: Heng wore the seal of Forward General for the Western Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Heng wore the seal of Forward General for the Western Campaign.

sentences.zh: 在鎮墾田積谷，邊備完固，自是大同希寇患。

translations.literal: While in command he opened fields and stored grain; frontier defenses were complete and secure, and from then on Datong rarely suffered from bandit troubles.
translations.idiomatic: While in command he opened fields and stored grain; frontier defenses were complete and secure, and from then on Datong rarely suffered from raids.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年召掌行後府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande he was recalled to manage affairs of the rear headquarters at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1 he was recalled to manage affairs of the rear headquarters at the mobile court.

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again commanded at Datong and transferred grain supplies to Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he again commanded at Datong and transferred grain supplies to Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 招降迤北部長四十九人，請於朝，厚撫之，歸附者相屬。

translations.literal: He induced forty-nine tribal chiefs of the northern frontier to submit, memorialized the court, and treated them generously; those who came over to allegiance followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He induced forty-nine tribal chiefs of the northern frontier to submit, memorialized the court, and treated them generously; those who came over to allegiance followed one after another.

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year he died in his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year he died in his command.

sentences.zh: 亨嚴肅重厚，善撫士卒，恥掊克。

translations.literal: Heng was stern, grave, and weighty in character, skilled at comforting troops, and ashamed of embezzling from them.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was stern, grave, and weighty in character, skilled at comforting his troops, and ashamed of skimming from them.

sentences.zh: 在大同時，鎮守中官撓軍政，亨裁之以理，其人不悅，然其卒也，深悼惜之。

translations.literal: While at Datong the eunuch superintendent interfered in military affairs; Heng restrained him with reason, and though the man was displeased, when Heng died he mourned him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: While at Datong the eunuch superintendent interfered in military affairs; Heng restrained him with reason. Though the man was displeased, when Heng died he mourned him deeply.

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhang with the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhang and given the posthumous title Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 妾張氏，自經以殉，贈淑人。

translations.literal: His concubine Lady Zhang hanged herself to follow him in death and was posthumously granted the title Shuren.
translations.idiomatic: His concubine Lady Zhang hanged herself to follow him in death and was posthumously granted the title Shuren.

translations.literal: His son Neng succeeded; the title was transmitted until Ming fell.
translations.idiomatic: His son Neng succeeded; the title passed down until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 徐忠，合肥人，襲父爵為河南衛副千戶。

translations.literal: Xu Zhong was a man of Hefei who inherited his father's title as deputy chiliarch of the Henan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhong came from Hefei and inherited his father's post as deputy chiliarch of the Henan Guard.

sentences.zh: 累從大軍北征，多所俘獲，進濟陽衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed the great army on northern campaigns, captured many prisoners, and was promoted to vice commander of the Jiyang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly joined the great army on northern campaigns, took many prisoners, and was promoted to vice commander of the Jiyang Guard.

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu he was stationed at Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Hongwu reign he was stationed at Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 燕兵破居庸、懷來，忠以開平降。

translations.literal: When the Yan army broke Juyong and Huailai, Zhong surrendered Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army broke Juyong and Huailai, Zhong surrendered Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 從徇灤河，與陳旭拔其城。

translations.literal: He followed in the drive on the Luan River and, with Chen Xu, captured its city.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the drive on the Luan River and, with Chen Xu, captured its city.

sentences.zh: 李景隆攻北平，燕師自大寧還救。

translations.literal: Li Jinglong attacked Beijing; the Yan army returned from Ning to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jinglong attacked Beijing, the Yan army returned from Ning to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 至會州，置五軍：張玉將中軍，朱能將左軍，李彬將右軍，房寬將後軍，忠號驍勇，使將前軍。

translations.literal: At Huizhou they established five armies: Zhang Yu commanded the center, Zhu Neng the left, Li Bin the right, Fang Kuan the rear; Zhong was famed for fierce valor and was made to command the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: At Huizhou they organized five armies: Zhang Yu commanded the center, Zhu Neng the left, Li Bin the right, Fang Kuan the rear; Zhong, famed for fierce valor, was placed in command of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 遂敗陳暉於白河，破景隆於鄭村壩。

translations.literal: He then defeated Chen Hui at the Bai River and broke Jinglong at Zhengcun Dam.
translations.idiomatic: He then defeated Chen Hui at the Bai River and routed Jinglong at Zhengcun Dam.

sentences.zh: 白溝河之戰，忠單騎突陣。

translations.literal: At the battle of Baigou River, Zhong charged the enemy lines alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Baigou River, Zhong charged the enemy lines alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 一指中流矢，未暇去鏃，急抽刀斷之。

translations.literal: One finger was struck by a stray arrow; he had no time to pull out the arrowhead and hastily drew his knife to cut it off.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck one of his fingers; with no time to pull out the head, he drew his knife and cut it off at once.

translations.literal: He spurred his horse at full gallop and fought a desperate battle.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse at full gallop and fought on to the death.

sentences.zh: 燕王乘高見之，謂左右曰：「真壯士也！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan, watching from high ground, said to those beside him, "A true stalwart!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan, watching from high ground, said to those beside him, "A true stalwart!"

sentences.zh: 進攻濟南，克滄州，大戰東昌、夾河。

translations.literal: He advanced on Jinan, captured Cangzhou, and fought great battles at Dongchang and Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Jinan, captured Cangzhou, and fought major battles at Dongchang and Jiahe.

sentences.zh: 攻彰德，破西水寨，克東阿、東平、汶上，大戰靈璧。

translations.literal: He attacked Zhangde, broke the West Water Stockade, captured Dong'e, Dongping, and Wenshang, and fought a great battle at Lingbi.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Zhangde, broke the West Water Stockade, captured Dong'e, Dongping, and Wenshang, and fought a great battle at Lingbi.

translations.literal: He then followed in crossing the Yangtze and entering the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed the army across the Yangtze and into the capital.

sentences.zh: 自指揮同知累遷都督僉事。

translations.literal: From vice commander he was promoted in stages to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: From vice commander he rose in stages to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 封永康侯，祿一千一百石，予世券。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang with an income of eleven hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang with an income of eleven hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 忠每戰，摧鋒跳蕩，為諸將先。

translations.literal: In every battle Zhong shattered the enemy vanguard and leapt through the ranks, going ahead of all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle Zhong shattered the enemy vanguard and plunged through the ranks ahead of all the other generals.

translations.literal: Yet he governed the army very strictly, and wherever he passed there was no disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he governed his troops with great strictness, and wherever he marched there was no disturbance.

translations.literal: He was skilled at comforting those who surrendered and won their utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at winning over those who surrendered and drew their utmost loyalty.

translations.literal: He was famed for filial devotion to his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for filial devotion to his stepmother.

translations.literal: When he returned at night he always bowed at the family shrine before entering.
translations.idiomatic: When he came home at night he always bowed at the family shrine before entering the house.

translations.literal: Frugal, restrained, and reverently careful, he never had a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal, restrained, and reverently careful, he was never known to err.

sentences.zh: 成祖北巡，以忠老成，留輔太子監國。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor toured the north, because Zhong was seasoned and steady he was left to assist the crown prince in supervising the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor toured the north, Zhong's seasoned steadiness led the emperor to leave him behind to assist the crown prince in supervising the state.

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year of Yongle he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of Yongle 11.

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Cai with the posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Cai and given the posthumous title Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 傳爵至裔孫錫登，崇禎末，死於賊。

translations.literal: The title was transmitted to his descendant Xideng; at the end of Chongzhen he died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed down to his descendant Xideng, who at the end of the Chongzhen reign was killed by rebels.

sentences.zh: 從兄錫胤嘗襲侯，卒，無子。

translations.literal: His cousin Xiyin had once succeeded to the marquisate; he died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Xiyin had once succeeded to the marquisate; he died without sons.

sentences.zh: 其妻朱氏，成國公純臣女也。

translations.literal: His wife was Lady Zhu, daughter of the Duke of Cheng Chunchen.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Lady Zhu, daughter of Duke of Cheng Chunchen.

sentences.zh: 夫歿，樓居十余年，不履地。

translations.literal: When her husband died she lived in an upper story for more than ten years without setting foot on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband died she lived in an upper story for more than ten years without setting foot on the ground.

translations.literal: When the city fell she embraced the ancestral tablets and burned herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell she embraced the ancestral tablets and burned herself to death.

sentences.zh: 子晟當嗣伯，仁宗特命嗣侯。

translations.literal: His son Sheng should have succeeded to the earldom, but Emperor Renzong specially ordered him to succeed to the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng should have succeeded to the earldom, but Emperor Renzong specially ordered him to succeed to the marquisate instead.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，坐扈駕先歸革爵，尋復之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande he was stripped of his title for returning ahead of the emperor while escorting the imperial procession, but soon had it restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 5 he was stripped of his title for returning ahead of the emperor while escorting the imperial procession, but soon had it restored.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟昂嗣伯，傳爵至明亡。

translations.literal: Having no sons, his younger brother Ang succeeded to the earldom; the title was transmitted until Ming fell.
translations.idiomatic: Having no sons, his younger brother Ang succeeded to the earldom; the title passed down until the dynasty fell.

translations.literal: Zhao Yi was a man of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi came from Hong.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，為燕山右衛百戶。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period he was a centurion in the Yan Mountain Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu period he served as a centurion in the Yan Mountain Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 從傅友德北征，城宣府、萬全、懷來，擢永平衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He followed Fu Youde on the northern campaign, helped fortify Xuanfu, Wanquan, and Huailai, and was promoted to vice commander of the Yongping Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fu Youde on the northern campaign, helped fortify Xuanfu, Wanquan, and Huailai, and was promoted to vice commander of the Yongping Guard.

sentences.zh: 降燕，歷諸戰皆有功，累遷都指揮使。

translations.literal: He surrendered to Yan; through successive battles he had merit in all of them and was promoted in stages to metropolitan commander.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered to the Prince of Yan; through battle after battle he earned merit and rose in stages to metropolitan commander.

sentences.zh: 成祖稱帝，封忻城伯，祿千石。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan became emperor he was enfeoffed as Earl of Xincheng with an income of a thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne he was enfeoffed as Earl of Xincheng with an income of a thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年，鎮宣府，嘗從北征。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongle he was stationed at Xuanfu and once followed the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 8 he was stationed at Xuanfu and once joined a northern campaign.

translations.literal: For embezzling provisions he was imprisoned and then released.
translations.idiomatic: For embezzling provisions he was imprisoned and then released.

sentences.zh: 尋以呂梁洪湍險，命彜鎮徐州經理。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, because the Lüliang rapids were dangerous in flood season, Yi was ordered to take command at Xuzhou to manage the works.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, because the Lüliang rapids were treacherous in flood season, Yi was ordered to take command at Xuzhou to manage the works.

sentences.zh: 復以擅殺運丁、盜官糧，為都御史李慶所劾。

translations.literal: Again, for killing transport laborers on his own authority and stealing official grain, he was impeached by the censor-in-chief Li Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for killing transport laborers on his own authority and stealing official grain, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Li Qing.

translations.literal: The judicial offices were ordered to try him, but he was again released.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices were ordered to try him, but he was again released.

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he was recalled.

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Xuande reign.

translations.literal: His son Rong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: After several generations the line reached Zhilong.
translations.idiomatic: Several generations later the line reached Zhilong.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，協守南京，大清兵下江南，之龍迎降。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen he helped defend Nanjing; when the Great Qing army descended on Jiangnan, Zhilong went out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign he helped defend Nanjing; when the Qing army descended on Jiangnan, Zhilong went out to surrender.

translations.literal: Zhang Xin was a man of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xin came from Linhuai.

translations.literal: His father Xing was vice commander of the Yongning Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xing was vice commander of the Yongning Guard.

sentences.zh: 信嗣官，移守普定、平越，積功進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Xin succeeded to the post, was transferred to hold Puding and Pingyue, and through accumulated merit was promoted to metropolitan vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xin succeeded to the post, was transferred to hold Puding and Pingyue, and through accumulated merit was promoted to metropolitan vice commander.

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was deeply grateful to Xin and called him "Kind Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor was deeply grateful to Xin and called him "Kind Zhang."

sentences.zh: 欲納信女為妃，信固辭，以此益見重。

translations.literal: He wished to take Xin's daughter as consort, but Xin firmly declined, and for this was all the more esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to take Xin's daughter as consort, but Xin firmly declined, and for this was all the more esteemed.

sentences.zh: 凡察藩王動靜諸密事，皆命信。

translations.literal: Whenever secret matters concerning the movements of princely domains were to be investigated, Xin was ordered to do it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever secret intelligence about the princely domains was needed, Xin was put in charge.

translations.literal: Xin, relying on favor, was rather arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on imperial favor, Xin grew rather arrogant.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年冬，都御史陳瑛言信「無汗馬勞，忝冒侯爵，恣肆貪墨，強占丹陽練湖八十餘里、江陰官田七十余頃，請下有司驗治。」

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year of Yongle the censor-in-chief Chen Ying said of Xin, "He has no merit of horses sweating in battle yet shamelessly holds a marquisate, acts wantonly and is corrupt, and forcibly occupies more than eighty li of the Danyang training lake and more than seventy qing of Jiangyin official fields; I request that the relevant offices verify and try him."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Yongle 8, Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying reported that Xin "has no merit of horses sweating in battle yet shamelessly holds a marquisate, acts wantonly and is corrupt, and forcibly occupies more than eighty li of the Danyang training lake and more than seventy qing of Jiangyin official fields; I request that the relevant offices verify and try him."

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Ying's words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ying is right.

sentences.zh: 昔中山王有沙洲一區，耕農水道所經，家僮阻之以擅利。

translations.literal: In former times the Prince of Zhongshan had a sandbank tract through which farming waterways passed, and his household slaves blocked it to monopolize profit.
translations.idiomatic: In former times the Prince of Zhongshan had a sandbank tract through which farming waterways passed, and his household slaves blocked it to monopolize the profit.

translations.literal: When the prince heard of it he at once returned the land to the government.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince heard of it he at once returned the land to the government.

translations.literal: How dare Xin do such a thing now!"
translations.idiomatic: How dare Xin do such a thing now!"

translations.literal: He ordered the judicial offices to try him on combined charges.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the judicial offices to try him on combined charges.

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, because of his old merit, he was not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, because of his old merit, he was not prosecuted.

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he followed the northern campaign and supervised transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he joined the northern campaign and supervised transport of provisions.

sentences.zh: 大閱於隰寧，信辭疾不至，謫充辦事官。

translations.literal: At the great review at Suining, Xin pleaded illness and did not attend; he was demoted to serve as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the great review at Suining, Xin pleaded illness and did not attend; he was demoted to serve as a staff officer.

translations.literal: Shortly afterward his post was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward his post was restored.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，加少師，並支二俸，與世侯券。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he was made Junior Preceptor, granted two salaries together, and given a hereditary marquis patent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he was made Junior Preceptor, granted two salaries together, and given a hereditary marquis patent.

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande he followed the campaign against Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1 he joined the campaign against Le'an.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝巡邊，征兀良哈，命居守。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor toured the frontier and campaigned against the Uriankhai; Xin was ordered to remain and hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor toured the frontier and campaigned against the Uriankhai; Xin was ordered to remain and hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年督軍萬五千人浚河西務河道。

translations.literal: The next year he supervised fifteen thousand troops in dredging the Hexiwu canal.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he supervised fifteen thousand troops in dredging the Hexiwu canal.

sentences.zh: 正統七年五月卒於南京。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Zhengtong he died at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Nanjing in the fifth month of Zhengtong 7.

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yun with the posthumous title Gongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yun and given the posthumous title Gongxi.

sentences.zh: 子鏞，自立功為指揮僉事，先卒。

translations.literal: His son Yong, who through his own merit had become vice commander, died first.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong, who through his own merit had become vice commander, died before him.

translations.literal: His son Chun succeeded; the title was transmitted until Ming fell.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun succeeded; the title passed down until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 有唐雲者，燕山中護衛指揮也，不知所自起。

translations.literal: There was a Tang Yun, commander of the Yan Mountain Central Guard, of whom it is not known whence he arose.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Tang Yun, commander of the Yan Mountain Central Guard, of whom it is not known whence he came.

sentences.zh: 成祖既殺張昺、謝貴等，將士猶據九門，閉甕城，陳戈戟內向。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Yan had killed Zhang Bing, Xie Gui, and others, the officers and soldiers still held the nine gates, closed the barbican gates, and arrayed spears and halberds facing inward.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince had killed Zhang Bing, Xie Gui, and others, the officers and soldiers still held the nine gates, closed the barbican gates, and arrayed spears and halberds facing inward.

sentences.zh: 張玉等夜襲之，已克其八，惟西直門不下。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu and others attacked by night; they had already taken eight gates, but Xizhi Gate would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu and others attacked by night; they had already taken eight gates, but Xizhi Gate would not fall.

sentences.zh: 成祖令雲解甲，騎馬導從如平時，諭守者曰：「天子已聽王自制一方。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan ordered Yun to remove his armor, ride on horseback and guide the procession as on ordinary days, and tell the defenders, "The Son of Heaven has already allowed the prince to rule a region on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The prince ordered Yun to remove his armor, ride on horseback and guide the procession as on ordinary days, and tell the defenders, "The Son of Heaven has already allowed the prince to rule a region on his own.

translations.literal: You must withdraw at once; those who come after will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: You must withdraw at once; those who linger will be executed."

sentences.zh: 雲於諸指揮中年最長，素信謹，將士以為不欺，遂散。

translations.literal: Yun was the eldest in years among the commanders, was always trusted and careful, and the officers and soldiers believed he would not deceive them, so they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was the eldest among the commanders, was always trusted and careful, and the officers and soldiers believed he would not deceive them, so they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 時眾心未附，雲告以天意所向，眾乃定。

translations.literal: At that time the hearts of the masses were not yet attached; Yun told them where Heaven's intent lay, and the masses then settled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time loyalty was still unsettled; Yun told them where Heaven's intent lay, and the troops then settled.

sentences.zh: 雲從成祖久，出入左右，甚見倚任。

translations.literal: Yun had long followed the Prince of Yan, going in and out at his side, and was greatly relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had long served at the prince's side and was greatly relied upon.

translations.literal: Whenever the prince went out on campaign he was left to assist the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prince marched out on campaign, Yun was left behind to assist the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 南兵數攻城，拒守甚力，戰未嘗失利。

translations.literal: The southern army repeatedly assaulted the city; he defended with great force and in battle never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The southern army repeatedly assaulted the city; he defended with great force and never lost a battle.

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to metropolitan commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to metropolitan commander.

sentences.zh: 成祖稱帝，封新昌伯，世指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan became emperor he was enfeoffed as Earl of Xinchang with hereditary metropolitan command.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became emperor he was enfeoffed as Earl of Xinchang with hereditary metropolitan command.

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the following year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of the following year.

translations.literal: The gifts bestowed on him were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The gifts bestowed on him were very generous.

translations.literal: His grandson Heng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Heng succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 十二年從北征，為中軍副將。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed the northern campaign as deputy commander of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he joined the northern campaign as deputy commander of the central army.

translations.literal: At the Tula River he captured three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tula River he captured three thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 還守開平，將輕騎往來興和、大同備邊。

translations.literal: On his return he held Kaiping and led light cavalry back and forth between Xinghe and Datong to prepare the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he held Kaiping and led light cavalry back and forth between Xinghe and Datong to prepare the frontier.

translations.literal: Afterward he repeatedly followed beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he repeatedly marched beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，以右副將征交阯，無功，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, as right deputy commander he campaigned against Jiaozhi without success and was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1, as right deputy commander he campaigned against Jiaozhi without success and was stripped of his title.

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne the title was restored.

sentences.zh: 正統九年，征兀良哈，出界嶺口、河北川，進侯。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengtong he campaigned against the Uriankhai, went out through Jieling Pass and Hebei River valley, and was promoted to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 9 he campaigned against the Uriankhai, went out through Jieling Pass and the Hebei River valley, and was promoted to marquis.

translations.literal: He went out to command in Shaanxi and was then recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He took command in Shaanxi and was then recalled.

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Tianshun and was given the posthumous title Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Tianshun reign and was given the posthumous title Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 子賢嗣伯，以跛免朝謁，給半祿，卒。

translations.literal: His son Xian succeeded to the earldom; because he was lame he was excused from court audience and given half salary; he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian succeeded to the earldom; because he was lame he was excused from court audience and given half salary; he died.

translations.literal: His son Sheng succeeded; he died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng succeeded; he died without sons.

translations.literal: His second cousin Liang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His second cousin Liang succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: Liang's paternal grandmother had been a former concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's paternal grandmother had been a former concubine.

translations.literal: His step-grandmother was the daughter of the Earl of Dingxiang Guo Deng.
translations.idiomatic: His step-grandmother was the daughter of Earl of Dingxiang Guo Deng.

translations.literal: At that point their grandsons disputed the succession.
translations.idiomatic: At that point their grandsons disputed the succession.

sentences.zh: 朝議以郭氏初嘗適人，法不當為正嫡，良竟得嗣。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that because the Guo lady had once been married to another man, by law she could not be the legitimate principal wife, and Liang ultimately obtained the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion held that because the Guo lady had once been married to another man, by law she could not be the legitimate principal wife, and Liang ultimately obtained the succession.

sentences.zh: 良時年五十，家貧，傭大中橋汲水。

translations.literal: Liang was then fifty years old, his family was poor, and he hired himself out at Dazhong Bridge to draw water.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was then fifty years old, his family was poor, and he hired himself out at Dazhong Bridge to draw water.

sentences.zh: 都督府求興安伯後，良乃謝其鄰而去，僉書南京中府。

translations.literal: The regional military commission sought a descendant of the Earl of Xing'an; Liang then thanked his neighbors and left, and was appointed secretary at the Nanjing central command.
translations.idiomatic: The regional military commission sought a descendant of the Earl of Xing'an; Liang then thanked his neighbors and left, and was appointed secretary at the Nanjing central command.

translations.literal: He offended Liu Jin and had two hundred piculs of his salary cut.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Liu Jin and had two hundred piculs of his salary cut.

translations.literal: The title was transmitted until the Ming fell.
translations.idiomatic: The title was transmitted until the Ming fell.

sentences.zh: 子隆，字彥平，年十五嗣封。

translations.literal: Zilong, styled Yanping, at age fifteen succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong, whose courtesy name was Yanping, succeeded to the title at the age of fifteen.

translations.literal: He was imposing in stature and possessed military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of imposing build with a gift for generalship.

sentences.zh: 數從北征，出奇料敵，成祖器之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed on northern campaigns, employing surprise and anticipating the enemy, and the Yongle Emperor valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in many northern campaigns, striking with surprise and reading the enemy well, and the Yongle Emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 即遷都，以南京根本地，命隆留守。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved, taking Nanjing as the foundational seat, he ordered Long to remain and guard it.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was moved, the emperor regarded Nanjing as the dynasty's foundation and ordered Long to remain there as garrison commander.

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, he was ordered to garrison Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Renzong came to the throne, he was appointed to command the garrison at Shanhaiguan.

translations.literal: Before long, he again guarded Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was once again posted to defend Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 隆讀書好文，論事侃侃，清慎守法，尤敬禮士大夫。

translations.literal: Long loved reading and literature, spoke forthrightly when discussing affairs, was pure and cautious in observing the law, and especially showed respect and courtesy to scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Long was a reader who loved letters; in council he spoke with easy confidence, and he was scrupulous and law-abiding, showing particular respect for the scholar-official class.

sentences.zh: 在南京十八年，前後賜璽書二百余。

translations.literal: During eighteen years at Nanjing, he was granted more than two hundred sealed imperial edicts in all.
translations.idiomatic: Over eighteen years in Nanjing, he received more than two hundred sealed edicts from the throne.

sentences.zh: 及召還，南都民流涕送之江上。

translations.literal: When he was recalled, the people of the southern capital wept as they saw him off on the river.
translations.idiomatic: When he was recalled to court, the people of the southern capital wept as they escorted him to the river.

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong he entered to take overall command of the imperial guard armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhengtong reign he was appointed to command the imperial guard armies.

sentences.zh: 十一年巡大同邊，賜寶刀一，申飭戒備，內外凜凜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he inspected the Datong frontier, was granted one precious sword, issued stern orders on defense preparedness, and both within and without were awed into discipline.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he inspected the Datong frontier, received an imperial sword, and issued stern orders on defense; throughout the command, officers and men alike were brought to strict attention.

translations.literal: When he finished and returned, he did not punish a single person.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned, he had not punished a single man.

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

translations.literal: His son Zhen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: He died at Tumu, was posthumously ennobled as marquis, and given the posthumous title Daoxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Tumu, was posthumously raised to marquis, and given the posthumous name Daoxi.

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

translations.literal: His younger brother Jin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jin succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 成化三年，四川都掌蠻叛，命佩征夷將軍印，充總兵官往討。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chenghua the Duzhang tribes of Sichuan rebelled; he was ordered to wear the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Yi and serve as overall commander to go and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chenghua, when the Duzhang tribes of Sichuan rose in rebellion, he was ordered to take the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Yi and go as overall commander to suppress them.

translations.literal: Minister of War Cheng Xin supervised the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of War, Cheng Xin, served as supervising secretary of the expedition.

translations.literal: When the army reached Yongning, it divided into six routes and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Yongning, it advanced in six columns.

sentences.zh: 瑾與信居中節制，盡破諸蠻寨。

translations.literal: Jin and Cheng, stationed at the center to coordinate, completely broke all the tribal stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Cheng directed operations from the center and overran every tribal stockade.

sentences.zh: 前後斬首四千五百有奇，獲鎧仗、牲畜無算。

translations.literal: In all they beheaded more than four thousand five hundred, and captured armor, weapons, and livestock beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than four thousand five hundred heads in all, along with incalculable quantities of armor, weapons, and livestock.

sentences.zh: 分都掌地，設官建治控制之。

translations.literal: They divided the Duzhang lands, established officials, and built administration to control them.
translations.idiomatic: They partitioned the Duzhang territory, appointed officials, and established civil administration to keep it under control.

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to marquis and repeatedly received additional appointments as Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was promoted to marquis and was repeatedly given the additional rank of Grand Protector.

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Hongzhi reign.

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Rui and given the posthumous title Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created Duke of Rui and given the posthumous name Zhuangwu.

translations.literal: Jin's nature was broad and magnanimous, and he was able to defer to men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was open-handed by nature and knew how to treat talented men with respect.

translations.literal: His elder brother Lian, because his appearance was inferior, was not permitted to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Lian was passed over for the succession on account of his unimpressive appearance.

translations.literal: Jin showed him very great respect and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Jin treated him with exceptional respect and generosity.

translations.literal: When Lian died, he nurtured his son Xi as if he were his own son.
translations.idiomatic: When Lian died, he raised Lian's son Xi as though the boy were his own.

translations.literal: Jin's son Fu succeeded to the earldom and died after several years.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's son Fu succeeded to the earldom but died within a few years.

translations.literal: Having no son, Xi obtained the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fu left no son, and Xi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 四傳至守锜，累典營務，加太子少保。

translations.literal: After four transmissions the line reached Shouqi, who repeatedly held camp duties and was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations later the line came down to Shouqi, who repeatedly commanded camp affairs and was given the additional rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，總督京營，坐營卒為盜落職，憂憤卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he governed the capital garrison, was dismissed from office because camp soldiers became bandits, and died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he was put in overall charge of the capital garrisons, but was removed from office when soldiers under his command turned to banditry; he died soon after, consumed by grief and anger.

translations.literal: His son Guozhen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guozhen succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: He had eloquence in speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fluent and persuasive speaker.

sentences.zh: 嘗召對，指陳兵事甚悉，帝信以為才。

translations.literal: Once summoned to audience, he pointed out and explained military affairs very thoroughly, and the emperor trusted that he had talent.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to audience, he laid out military matters in exhaustive detail, and the emperor came to believe he was a man of real ability.

sentences.zh: 十六年命總督京營，倚任之，而國禎實無他能。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was ordered to govern the capital garrison and was relied upon, but Guozhen in truth had no other ability.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed to command the capital garrisons and was heavily relied upon, though in fact Guozhen had no other talent to speak of.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，李自成犯京師。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year Li Zicheng attacked the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following March, Li Zicheng marched on the capital.

translations.literal: The soldiers of the three great camps collapsed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The troops of the three great garrisons broke and fled without offering battle.

translations.literal: After two nights the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the city fell.

sentences.zh: 賊勒國禎降，國禎解甲聽命。

translations.literal: The rebels forced Guozhen to surrender; Guozhen removed his armor and obeyed their command.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels demanded that Guozhen submit; he laid down his arms and awaited their orders.

sentences.zh: 責賄不足，被拷折踝，自縊死。

translations.literal: They demanded bribes that were insufficient, tortured him until his ankles were broken, and he hanged himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: When his bribes proved insufficient they tortured him until his ankles were broken, and he hanged himself.

translations.literal: Sun Yan was a man of Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yan was a native of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 從太祖渡江，累官燕山中護衛千戶，致仕。

translations.literal: He followed the Taizu Emperor in crossing the Yangzi, rose through repeated appointments to battalion commander of the Yanzhong Central Guard, and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the founding emperor across the Yangzi, rose through the ranks to battalion commander of the Yanzhong Central Guard, and then retired.

sentences.zh: 燕師起，通州守將房勝以城降。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan's army rose, Fang Sheng, the defending general of Tongzhou, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan raised his army, Fang Sheng, the garrison commander at Tongzhou, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 王以巖宿將，使與勝協守。

translations.literal: The prince, because Yan was a veteran general, had him join Fang Sheng in jointly defending the place.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, knowing Yan to be a seasoned commander, put him alongside Fang Sheng to hold the city together.

sentences.zh: 南軍至，攻城甚急，樓堞皆毀。

translations.literal: When the southern army arrived, it pressed the siege fiercely and destroyed all the parapets and battlements.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern army arrived, it assaulted the city with great urgency and smashed the walls and towers.

translations.literal: Yan and Fang defended by every means.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Fang held the city by every means they could devise.

sentences.zh: 已，復突門力戰，追奔至張家灣，獲餉舟三百。

translations.literal: Later they again burst through the gate and fought fiercely, pursued the fleeing enemy to Zhangjiawan, and captured three hundred supply boats.
translations.idiomatic: Later they sallied through the gate and fought hard, pursued the retreating enemy as far as Zhangjiawan, and seized three hundred supply boats.

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice commander of the regional military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to vice commander of the regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 論功，以舊臣有守城功，封應城伯，祿千石。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, because as an old minister he had merit in defending the city, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Yingcheng with an income of one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were distributed, he was created Earl of Yingcheng with an income of one thousand piculs in recognition of his service as a veteran who had held the city.

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年，備開平，旋移通州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongle he prepared defenses at Kaiping, then was soon transferred to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongle he took charge of defenses at Kaiping, and was soon afterward reassigned to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以私憾椎殺千戶，奪爵，安置交阯。

translations.literal: Because of a personal grudge he bludgeoned a battalion commander to death, was stripped of his title, and was resettled in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He bludgeoned a battalion commander to death over a private grievance, lost his title, and was exiled to Jiaozhi.

translations.literal: Before long his title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his title was restored.

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year.

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled as marquis and given the posthumous title Weiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously raised to marquis and given the posthumous name Weiwu.

translations.literal: His son Heng succeeded; the title was transmitted until the Ming fell, and then the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng succeeded to the title, which passed down until the fall of the Ming, when the enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 子智，前立功為常山右護衛指揮，嗣父爵。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, who had earlier achieved merit as commander of the Changshan Right Guard, succeeded to his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, who had earlier distinguished himself as commander of the Changshan Right Guard, succeeded to his father's title.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，以參將佩征夷將軍印，鎮交阯。

translations.literal: During the Xuande reign he served as vice general wearing the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Yi and garrisoned Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign he was posted to Jiaozhi as vice general with the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Yi.

sentences.zh: 怯不任戰，又與都督方政相失。

translations.literal: He was timid and unfit for battle, and he also fell out with the regional commander Fang Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He proved too timid for combat and also fell out with the regional commander Fang Zheng.

translations.literal: Le Loi's power was strong; he could not resist and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Le Loi's forces were in the ascendant; Zhi could not hold them back and was routed.

translations.literal: He was stripped of his title and reduced to probationary officer status.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his title and reduced to serving as a probationary officer.

translations.literal: He followed Wang Tong and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Wang Tong and won distinction.

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because the territory was abandoned and he returned, he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon thrown into prison for abandoning the territory and returning home.

translations.literal: He was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually released.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he was again made guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengtong reign he was restored to the rank of guard commander.

translations.literal: Zhang Xing was a man of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing was a native of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 起卒伍，為燕山左護衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Rising from the ranks, he became vice commander of the Yanshan Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to become vice commander of the Yanshan Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 從起兵，功多，累遷都指揮同知。

translations.literal: He followed in raising the army, achieved many merits, and was repeatedly promoted to assistant commander of the regional military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the prince in raising his army, won many honors, and rose through repeated promotions to assistant commander of the regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 從子勇，有力敢戰，從興行陣為肘腋。

translations.literal: His nephew Yong was strong and bold in battle, followed Xing in the ranks, and served at his side.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yong was powerful and fearless in battle and marched at Xing's side as his right-hand man.

sentences.zh: 興嘗單騎追敵，被數十創，傷重不任戰。

translations.literal: Xing once pursued the enemy alone on horseback, received several dozen wounds, and was too gravely injured to continue fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Xing once charged the enemy alone and took several dozen wounds; his injuries were so severe that he could no longer take the field.

sentences.zh: 以勇嗣指揮使，代將其兵。

translations.literal: Yong succeeded to the post of guard commander and took command of his troops in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Yong succeeded him as guard commander and took over command of his troops.

translations.literal: When merits were assessed again, Xing was enfeoffed as Earl of Anxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were reckoned again, Xing was created Earl of Anxiang.

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Yongle he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the fifth year of Yongle.

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

translations.literal: Yong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年從北征，失律，謫交阯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongle he followed the northern campaign, violated military discipline, and was banished to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongle he joined the northern campaign, broke discipline, and was exiled to Jiaozhi.

translations.literal: He was pardoned and returned, his title was restored, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned, allowed to return, and had his title restored before he died.

translations.literal: His son An succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son An succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he garrisoned Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he was posted to command Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 黃蕭養寇廣州，安帥舟師遇賊於戙船澳。

translations.literal: Huang Xiaoyang raided Guangzhou; An led the fleet and encountered the bandits at Dangchuan Bay.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Xiaoyang threatened Guangzhou, An led the fleet and met the rebels at Dangchuan Bay.

sentences.zh: 安方醉臥，官軍不能支，退至沙角尾。

translations.literal: An was at the time drunk and asleep; the government troops could not hold, and retreated to Shajiaowei.
translations.idiomatic: An was drunk and asleep at the time; the government forces could not stand their ground and fell back to Shajiaowei.

translations.literal: The bandits pressed close upon them and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed the attack and the army broke in rout.

translations.literal: An drowned and died.
translations.idiomatic: An drowned.

translations.literal: The title was transmitted down to Guangcan, who died at the hands of roving bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed down to Guangcan, who was killed by roving bandits.

translations.literal: Chen Zhi was a man of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi was a native of Ba.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，為燕山中護衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he served as vice commander of the Yanzhong Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign he served as vice commander of the Yanzhong Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 從起兵，累遷都指揮同知，封遂安伯。

translations.literal: He followed in raising the army, was repeatedly promoted to assistant commander of the regional military commission, and was enfeoffed as Earl of Suian.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the prince in raising his army, rose through repeated promotions to assistant commander of the regional military commission, and was created Earl of Suian.

sentences.zh: 誌素以恭謹受知，戮力戎行，始終不懈。

translations.literal: Zhi had long been known for respectful care, exerted his strength in military campaigns, and from beginning to end never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had long been valued for his respectful diligence; he gave his full strength on campaign and never slackened from first to last.

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Yongle he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the eighth year of Yongle.

translations.literal: His grandson Ying succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Ying succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 屢從出塞，鎮永平、山海、薊州，城雲州、獨石。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns beyond the frontier, garrisoned Yongping, Shanhai, and Jizhou, and fortified Yunzhou and Dushi.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in many campaigns beyond the frontier, held garrisons at Yongping, Shanhai, and Jizhou, and built fortifications at Yunzhou and Dushi.

translations.literal: He was open and broad-minded and possessed the talent of a general.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed by nature and showed real talent as a commander.

translations.literal: Yet he was greedy and cruel, and many people resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy and brutal, and many under his command resented him.

translations.literal: When he died, his son Xun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Xun succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: He died at Tumu and was given the posthumous title Ronghuai.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Tumu and was given the posthumous name Ronghuai.

translations.literal: His younger brother Shao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shao succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

translations.literal: His grandson Xian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Xian succeeded to the title.

translations.literal: He commanded the troops of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took overall command of the Jizhou garrison.

translations.literal: When the Tümed raided he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tümed raided, he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，敘奉迎功，加太子太保，進少保，委寄亞武定侯郭勛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was rewarded for merit in welcoming the throne, was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, advanced to Junior Guardian, and entrusted with responsibilities second only to the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he was rewarded for helping welcome the new emperor, was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, advanced to Junior Guardian, and entrusted with responsibilities second only to Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun.

translations.literal: He succeeded to the earldom for more than sixty years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He held the earldom for more than sixty years before he died.

translations.literal: After five more generations Ming fell.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations later the dynasty fell.

translations.literal: Wang You was a man of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang You came from Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 襲父職為燕山護衛百戶。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post as centurion of the Yan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post as centurion of the Yan Guard.

translations.literal: He followed in raising troops and pacified the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the rebellion and helped secure the capital.

sentences.zh: 論功當侯，以驕縱，授都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he should have been made a marquis, but because of arrogance and license he was given only metropolitan vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: By merit he should have been made a marquis, but because of arrogance and license he received only the post of metropolitan vice commander.

sentences.zh: 及丘福等議上，乃封清遠伯。

translations.literal: When Qiu Fu and others presented their deliberations to the throne, he was then enfeoffed as Earl of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu Fu and others presented their recommendations, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年充總兵官，帥舟師沿海捕倭。

translations.literal: The next year he served as supreme commander, leading a fleet along the coast to hunt pirates.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he served as supreme commander, leading a fleet along the coast against the pirates.

sentences.zh: 倭數掠海上，友無功，帝切責之。

translations.literal: The pirates repeatedly raided along the sea; You achieved nothing, and the emperor sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates repeatedly raided the coast; You achieved nothing, and the emperor sharply rebuked him.

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he inflicted a great defeat on the pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he inflicted a crushing defeat on the pirates.

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, issued an edict of praise and reward, and soon recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, issued an edict praising and rewarding him, and soon recalled him.

sentences.zh: 四年從征交阯，與指揮柳琮合兵破籌江柵，困枚、普賴諸山，斬首三萬七千余級。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the campaign against Jiaozhi; together with Commander Liu Cong he united forces to break the Choujiang stockade, penned the enemy in the mountains of Mei, Pulai, and others, and took more than thirty-seven thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined the campaign against Jiaozhi; together with Commander Liu Cong he united forces to break the Choujiang stockade, penned the enemy in the mountains of Mei, Pulai, and others, and took more than thirty-seven thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 六年七月進侯，加祿五百石，與世券。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was advanced to marquis, given an additional five hundred piculs of income, and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was advanced to marquis, given an additional five hundred piculs of income, and granted a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 明年，再征交阯，為副總兵。

translations.literal: The next year he campaigned against Jiaozhi again as deputy supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he campaigned against Jiaozhi again as deputy supreme commander.

translations.literal: In the eighth year he returned; he followed the northern campaign and supervised the central army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he returned, joined the northern campaign, and supervised the central army.

sentences.zh: 別與劉才築城飲馬河上。

translations.literal: Separately, together with Liu Cai, he built a fort on the Yinma River.
translations.idiomatic: Separately, together with Liu Cai, he built a fort on the Yinma River.

sentences.zh: 會知院失乃幹欲降，帝令友將士卒先行，諭以遇敵相機剿滅。

translations.literal: It happened that the court official Shinagan wished to surrender; the emperor ordered You to lead the troops forward first and instructed him that on encountering the enemy he should destroy them as circumstances allowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the court official Shinagan wished to surrender, the emperor ordered You to lead the troops forward first and instructed him to destroy the enemy whenever opportunity allowed.

sentences.zh: 友等至，與敵相距一程，迂道避之應昌。

translations.literal: When You and the others arrived they were one stage's march from the enemy, but took a detour to avoid them and went to Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: When You and the others arrived they were one day's march from the enemy, but took a detour to avoid them and went to Yingchang.

translations.literal: The army lacked food and many died.
translations.idiomatic: The army ran short of food and many men died.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，屢旨切責，奪其軍屬張輔。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, repeatedly sent edicts of sharp rebuke, and transferred his army to Zhang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, sent repeated edicts of sharp rebuke, and transferred his army to Zhang Fu.

translations.literal: On his return he ordered the ministers to deliberate on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he ordered the ministers to deliberate on his punishment.

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 十二年，坐妾告友夫婦誹謗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was implicated because a concubine accused You and his wife of slander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year a concubine accused You and his wife of slander, and he was implicated.

translations.literal: The charge was verified and his title was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: The charge was verified and his title was taken away.

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，官其子順為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he appointed his son Shun vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne he appointed his son Shun vice commander.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：張武、陳珪諸人，或從起藩封，或率先歸附，皆偏裨列校，非有勇略智計稱大將材也。

translations.literal: The praise says: Zhang Wu, Chen Gui, and the others either followed the prince from the rise of his princely fief or were the first to submit; all were staff officers and company commanders, without courage, strategy, or wisdom that would qualify them as material for great generals.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal runs: Zhang Wu, Chen Gui, and the others either followed the prince from the rise of his princely fief or were among the first to submit. All were staff officers and company commanders, without the courage, strategy, or wisdom that would mark them as great generals.

sentences.zh: 一旦遘風雲之會，剖符策功，號稱佐命，與太祖開國諸臣埒，酬庸之義不亦厚歟！

translations.literal: Yet once they met the moment when wind and cloud gathered, they received investiture and were recorded for merit, were styled assistants in founding the dynasty, and were ranked with the ministers who founded the dynasty under Taizu — is not the meaning of rewarding merit exceedingly generous!
translations.idiomatic: Yet once fortune turned their way they received investiture, were recorded for merit, were styled founders of the new reign, and were ranked with Taizu's ministers who built the dynasty — was not the court exceedingly generous in rewarding their service!
